paper.abstract_en: The field of Deep Inelastic Scattering is introduced with particular reference to the High Energy Ring Accelerator HERA. The formalism of the Quark Parton Model and its extension in perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics is outlined, defining the concept of a Parton Distribution Function. The HERA data on inclusive and semi-inclusive processes are reviewed with particular emphasis on results at low x and low Q 2 . Their theoretical imterpretation in terms of conventional QCD DGLAP evolution and its extension to BFKL evolution in the low-x regime is explored together with the possibility of the onset of a new non-linear regime which may lead to gluon saturation. The focus then moves to diffractive processes both quasi-elastic and diffractive dissociation, where more detailed hints of saturation are found.
